chapter_theme: Truth, knowledge and bliss (சத்திய ஞானானந்தம்): passing beyond the three voids and the states into the turiya of 'thou' and 'that', the knower sheds malam and the thirty-six tattvas and becomes Siva. The qualities of the Supreme, truth and the rest, stand together as a water lily's form, colour, scent and beauty; the bliss floods the body like milk and honey, and even the thought of the Lord is his grace.
structure_note: Beyond the voids and the third turiya (2825, 2826); the water-lily image for the Supreme's qualities (2827 to 2829); grace and the flood of turiya (2830, 2831); the Lord beyond and the jnani's attainment (2832 to 2834). The grouping is mine.

2825.reading: Becoming every void, void and all things and yet not them, attending to the three voids and the three voids below, the one who is supreme knowledge-bliss becomes That, in a bliss where there is no saying 'this void is so'.
2825.nuance: பாழ் (void, emptiness) and முப்பாழ் (the three voids) are technical terms in the ninth tantra; they are traditionally taken as voids of the soul, of maya and of the Supreme (or of the three padas of 'that thou art'), but the verse does not list them. கீழுள முப்பாழ் (the three voids below) suggests two sets of three.

2826.reading: Like the turiya spoken of 'thou' and 'that', it becomes good in the trusted third turiya; beyond the beautiful earth and the unthought super-subtle is the perfect thing, glorious Nandi, who rules and gives grace.
2826.nuance: தொம்பதம் (thou) and தற்பதம் (that) are the words of the great saying 'that thou art', each given its own turiya in the earlier chapters; the third turiya is traditionally that of அசி (art), their union. அம்புவி யுன்னா may be divided differently.

2827.reading: To compare the lasting truth and the rest with the stainless light of a gem does not fit; rather, like the fresh water lily with its form, bright colour, fragrance and beauty, they are spoken of as six.
2827.nuance: சத்தியாதி (truth and the rest) is taken as truth, knowledge, bliss and the qualities that go with them; the count of six (ஆறும்) is not explained. மாசோயை is obscure. The point seems to be that the qualities are distinct yet inseparable, like a flower's form, colour and scent, not one undivided glow.

2828.reading: When Shakti, Siva and supreme knowledge are spoken of, the endless one given, Siva who is high bliss, the Shakti of his own form, the guru who comes and the body given are like the water lily.
2828.nuance: The list is compressed and its grouping uncertain. The water lily (உற்பலம்) again stands for distinct aspects that cannot be separated; that the guru and the body are among them suggests the Lord's coming as guru in a body is one with his nature.

2829.reading: As the water lily's form, colour, bright fragrance and beauty stand together, so when the soul merges in the Supreme, he stands so that truth and the rest appear in the very form of the great three padas called Siva.
2829.nuance: மாமுப்பதம் (the great three padas) are taken as 'thou', 'that' and 'art'. The verse makes the water lily image explicit and applies it to the soul's union, not to the Lord alone.

2830.reading: If one bows with a melting heart as far as one can think, and adorns him, one can hold him within; Nandi my king, joining his grace even to me, made me think as far as I think.
2830.nuance: The verse turns on நினையும் அளவில் (as far as one thinks), used twice: first as the measure of the devotee's worship, then as the measure of what the Lord's grace made him think. Even the thinking is given. பொதியல் (to contain, to wrap) may also mean to enshrine.

2831.reading: Like honey with milk, the juice within fruit and the sweetness of the great pure nectar, turiya, when it enters, floods the virtuous through every hair-root.
2831.nuance: பொடிபடி is obscure: perhaps 'shattering' or 'settling like fine dust'. சீல (virtuous) may qualify the person or be part of a phrase about the body. The bliss is felt in the body, at every மயிர்க்கால், not only in the mind.

2832.reading: Passing beyond the immortal state and beyond the cosmos, the Lord who stands alone in the beyond stood following the unwavering light of the woman with pearls in coral and cool speech.
2832.nuance: The woman with pearl teeth in coral lips and cool words is taken as Shakti. தமரம் (sound, or a hollow) is obscure, as is whether the light is hers or his own that she follows.

2833.reading: Changing the middle thirty-six, removing malam, becoming pure and free of flaw in turiya, losing bondage and becoming Siva, and so transformed, the jnani reaches truth, knowledge and bliss.
2833.nuance: ஆறாறு is the thirty-six tattvas; மத்திமம் (middle) may refer to the middle state or channel. பெத்தம் is bondage (baddha), the opposite of release. பிறழ்வுற்றும் (even turning aside, changing) is unclear.

2834.reading: Becoming Siva so that the three disgraceful malas end, holding the three voids of birth so as to cling no more, in the truth, knowledge and bliss that is austerity, the turiya full of 'thou' is the true form itself.
2834.nuance: பவமான முப்பாழ் (the three voids that are birth) and பற்றறப் பற்ற (to hold so as to cling no more) are paradoxical and technical. துவம் is taken as tvam, 'thou'. The last line seems short of a syllable or two.

links.note: In 2592 the Lord takes the poet into himself like water into hot iron and swallows the light of the three voids; 2825 describes the bliss of one who has gone past the three voids into supreme knowledge-bliss.
2437 names the three padas, 'thou', 'that' and 'art', which bring one to Siva; 2826 gives each its turiya and puts the good in the third.

The water lily (உற்பலம்) whose form, colour, scent and beauty cannot be separated: in 2829 for truth and the rest in the soul's union, in 2843 for the guru in whom form and quality are swallowed into the true form.

2483 uses a gem's stone-light, colour, lustre and rays (கல்லொளி மாநிறம் சோபை கதிர்) as the image of experience in the three voids; 2827 says comparing truth and the rest to a stainless gem's light does not fit (மணியொளி ... ஒப்பம் இடல் ஒன்றா) and offers the water lily's form, colour, fragrance and beauty instead. On this reading 2827 limits the gem simile: a gem's glow is one, while the qualities are distinct yet inseparable like the lily's.

2828 likens Shakti, Siva-bliss, the coming guru and the given body to the water lily (உற்பலம் போலுமே); 2843 again uses the lily (உற்பலம் ஆமாறு போல) for the guru of true form (சொரூபக்குரவன்) who holds truth and the rest. In both the lily's inseparable aspects carry the claim that the guru is not apart from the Lord's own nature.

Kural 396 says understanding wells up as far as one has learned (கற்றனைத் தூறும் அறிவு), as water does in a sand well as far as it is dug. 2830 uses the same measure, நினையும் அளவில் (as far as one thinks), but ends that Nandi, joining his grace, made him think as far as he thinks (நினைப்பித்தனனே). The Kural puts the measure in one's effort; the Tirumanthiram says even that measure is given.

2834 speaks of holding the three voids that are birth (பவமான முப்பாழ்) so as to cling no more, ending in true form; 2496 names the three voids: the void of maya is the soul, the void of space the Supreme, the third the soul pervaded in Siva-Shakti, ending where speech ends in pure form (தூய சொரூபத்தில்). 2496 supplies the scheme that 2834 assumes.

source_issues: 2827: மாசோயை in line 1 is obscure and may be corrupt.
2834: line 4 (துவமார் துரியம் சொரூபம் தாமே) appears short and may have lost a word.
